name: Error Recovery
summary: Turn generation failures — timeouts, refusals, tool errors — into recoverable moments by preserving the user's input and always offering a way forward.
problem: AI systems fail often and opaquely: network timeouts, context overflows, safety refusals, tool errors. A bare 'Something went wrong' plus a discarded prompt converts a recoverable hiccup into abandoned work, and treating a refusal like a server error sends users down the wrong recovery path.
useWhen: Generation can fail for reasons the user can act on: rephrasing, retrying, shortening input
The user invested effort in a prompt or draft that must survive the failure
Failures have distinguishable causes that warrant different recovery paths
dontUseWhen: Failures are programmatic and retried silently with no user decision required
The surrounding platform already owns failure UI and duplicating it would conflict
There is genuinely no user-side recovery action, where a status surface is more honest than fake options

anatomy.description: Plain-language statement of what happened and what the user can do about it.
One or more concrete next steps: retry, edit and resend, switch approach.
The user's prompt or draft, retained and editable after the failure.
Expandable technical detail — error codes, raw messages — for users who want it.

states.description: A failure occurred; summary, preserved input, and recovery actions are shown.
A recovery action is in flight; controls reflect the busy state.
The retry succeeded; normal output flow resumes.

constraints.statement: The user's input MUST be preserved and remain editable after any failure.
constraints.rationale: Retyping a lost prompt is the most expensive possible outcome of a transient failure; preserved input makes every other recovery path cheap.
constraints.verification: E2E test: force a failure mid-request and assert the prompt text is intact and editable.

constraints.statement: Every error state MUST present at least one recovery action.
constraints.rationale: A terminal message with no action strands the user; even 'try again later' with a retry control beats a dead end.
constraints.verification: Unit test: every entry in the error taxonomy maps to one or more rendered recovery actions.

constraints.statement: The error summary MUST describe what happened in plain language, with raw codes and technical detail relegated to the detail region.
constraints.rationale: Users cannot act on 'Error 529'; they can act on 'The service is overloaded — try again in a minute'.
constraints.verification: Manual review of summary copy for each error kind; codes appear only inside the detail disclosure.

constraints.statement: Failures MUST be announced to assistive technology through an assertive live region or alert role.
constraints.rationale: A visual-only error leaves screen reader users waiting on a response that will never arrive.
constraints.verification: Unit test: the error summary container has role=alert (or aria-live assertive) and its content updates on failure.

constraints.statement: While a retry is in flight, the component MUST prevent duplicate submissions and expose the busy state accessibly.
constraints.rationale: Anxious double-clicks on retry produce duplicate side effects and duplicate charges.
constraints.verification: Unit test: activating retry twice while in flight invokes the retry callback once; the control exposes aria-disabled or aria-busy.

constraints.statement: Safety refusals SHOULD be distinguished from technical failures, with recovery paths that fit the cause: rephrase for refusals, retry for transient errors.
constraints.rationale: Retrying a refusal verbatim cannot succeed and teaches users the system is arbitrary; rephrasing a timeout wastes effort.
constraints.verification: Unit test: refusal-kind errors render rephrase-oriented actions, transient-kind errors render retry.

constraints.statement: Implementations MAY automatically retry transient failures once with backoff, with visible indication, before surfacing the error.
constraints.rationale: Many infrastructure blips resolve in seconds; one silent-but-indicated retry saves an interruption without hiding persistent failure.
constraints.verification: Code review: auto-retry is bounded, indicated in the UI, and falls through to the error state.

wcagCriteria.name: Error Identification
wcagCriteria.relevance: The failure must be identified and described to the user in text.

wcagCriteria.name: Error Suggestion
wcagCriteria.relevance: Recovery actions are the suggestion mechanism: known fixes must be offered to the user.

wcagCriteria.name: Status Messages
wcagCriteria.relevance: Retry progress and recovery results are status changes that must reach assistive technology.

keyboard.action: Reaches each recovery action and the preserved input in document order.

screenReader.behavior: Assertive announcement of the plain-language summary.
Polite announcement of retry progress and its outcome.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focus is not stolen on failure; the alert announcement carries the information and the user navigates to recovery actions on their own terms.
accessibility.reducedMotion: No shake or flash effects on error under prefers-reduced-motion; static styling communicates the failure.

do: Write summaries as 'what happened + what to do': 'The request timed out. Your prompt is saved — try again.'
Keep the failed request's partial output visible if any arrived before the failure.
Offer 'edit and resend' as a first-class action, not just bare retry.
dont: Do not clear or disable the user's input while showing an error.
Do not present a refusal with a retry button as the primary action.
Do not stack multiple error banners for one failure; replace, don't append.
